title: ALMA-IMF: XV. Core mass function in the high-mass star formation regime
question: Measure the core mass function (CMF) at a homogeneous physical resolution of 2700 au across 15 Milky Way high-mass protoclusters and test whether its high-mass slope differs from the canonical Salpeter IMF slope (α = 2.35).

data.angular_resolution: Native Band 6: 0.31" to 0.90" (1365 to 2685 au); smoothed Band 6 and Band 3: 0.49" to 1.35" (matched 2700 au)
data.sensitivity: Native Band 6: 9 to 60 mK; Native Band 3: 3 to 26 mK; Smoothed Band 6: 0.06 to 0.52 mJy/beam

what.value: Phase center coordinates, evolutionary stages, and distances of the 15 protoclusters

evidence.quote: (1) Phase center, evolutionary stage and distance to the region taken from Tables 1 and 4 of Paper I.

what.value: Central frequencies in Band 6 and Band 3 and cleanest 1.3 mm and 3 mm continuum emission maps

evidence.quote: Since we wish to assemble the most reliable sample of cores, we use the cleanest continuum maps, publicly available on the ALMA-IMF website
(2) Central frequencies in Band 6 (≃1.3 mm) and in Band 3 (≃3.0 mm) taken from Table D.1 of Paper II.

what.value: PPMAP dust temperature maps at 2.5" angular resolution for the 15 ALMA-IMF protoclusters

evidence.quote: Following the pilot study by Motte et al. (2018), we used the Bayesian procedure _PPMAP_ (Marsh et al. 2015; Dell’Ova et al. 2024) to build the temperature maps of the ALMA-IMF protoclusters.

what.value: Hot core candidates identified via methyl formate emission maps and their assigned temperature of 100±50 K (and 300±100 K for G327.29 source n°1)

evidence.quote: Following the method discussed in Bonfand et al. (2024), we set 100±50 K to the 49 sources whose position corresponds to the peaks of extended methyl formate emission

Additionally, we set 300±100 K to sources n [◦] 1, n [◦] 2, and n [◦] 1 in W51-IRS2, W51-E and G327.29 respectively, following their detailed modelling by Ginsburg et al. (2017), Goddi et al. (2020), and the adopted temperature in Bonfand et al. (2024), respectively.

what.value: Detailed temperature modelling (300±100 K) for hot core sources n°1 in W51-IRS2 and n°2 in W51-E

evidence.quote: Additionally, we set 300±100 K to sources n [◦] 1, n [◦] 2, and n [◦] 1 in W51-IRS2, W51-E and G327.29 respectively, following their detailed modelling by Ginsburg et al. (2017), Goddi et al. (2020), and the adopted temperature in Bonfand et al. (2024), respectively.

external_data.citation: Ginsburg et al. (2017); Goddi et al. (2020)

recipe.goal: Smooth continuum maps to matched physical resolution
recipe.method: Convolve the 1.3 mm (Band 6) and 3 mm (Band 3) cleanest continuum maps of all 15 fields with a Gaussian kernel to achieve a homogeneous spatial resolution of 2700 au.
key_parameters: Target spatial resolution = 2700 au; Gaussian kernel width θ_conv = sqrt((2700 au / D)^2 - θ_native^2)
assumptions: Distances D to each protocluster from Paper I (2000 to 5500 pc)

recipe.goal: Extract compact continuum sources and compare algorithms
recipe.method: Two-step extraction on both native and 2700 au smoothed maps using getsf and GExt2D: detect source candidates on 1.3 mm maps without primary beam correction, then measure fluxes and sizes on 1.3 mm and 3 mm maps after primary beam correction.

recipe.goal: Filter out free-free contaminated sources using 1.3 mm and 3 mm spectral indices
recipe.method: Rescale 3 mm integrated fluxes for 1.3 mm vs 3 mm source size differences, compute spectral index γ (Eq. 2), and reject sources with γ < 2. For sources undetected by getsf at 3 mm but lying on pixel-by-pixel spectral index map regions with γ < 2 (3 mm background > 3σ), measure aperture upper-limit 3 mm flux (Eq. 3) and reject those with γ < 1.
key_parameters: Rejection thresholds: γ < 2 for sources detected at 3 mm (68 rejected); γ < 1 for 3 mm aperture upper limits on free-free background (16 rejected).
assumptions: Linear 3 mm flux rescaling with source axes works for optically thick emission or optically thin isothermal envelope with density profile ρ(r) ∝ r^-2.

recipe.goal: Assign dust temperatures to each core
recipe.method: Assign per-core dust temperatures from 2.5" resolution PPMAP Bayesian SED fitting maps (combining free-free decontaminated ALMA Band 6, SOFIA/HAWC+, Herschel PACS/SPIRE, and APEX SABOCA/LABOCA), overriding with 100±50 K for 49 methyl formate hot core candidates and 300±100 K for 3 extreme hot cores.
key_parameters: PPMAP angular resolution = 2.5"; temperature uncertainty = 25% (or 5 K for T < 20 K); hot core T = 100±50 K or 300±100 K.
assumptions: Methyl formate (CH3OCHO) sublimates from dust grains at ~100 K and traces internal heating in hot cores.

recipe.goal: Derive core masses and evaluate gravitational boundedness
recipe.method: Convert 1.3 mm integrated and peak fluxes to core mass using Eq. 4 (with first-order optical depth correction), and evaluate gravitational boundedness using the critical Bonnor-Ebert mass ratio M_BE / M_core < 2.
key_parameters: Boundedness threshold: M_BE / M_source < 2; M_BE = 2.4 * R * σ_th^2 / G; R = (a * b^2)^(1/3) * D.
assumptions: Dust + gas opacity per unit mass κ_1.3mm = 0.1 * (ν / 1000 GHz)^β cm^2 g^-1 with β = 1.5 (Ossenkopf & Henning 1994); isothermal adiabatic index γ = 1; mean molecular weight per free particle µ = 2.4.

recipe.goal: Determine mass completeness limits per field via synthetic core injection
recipe.method: Inject synthetic 2D circular Gaussian cores (FWHM = 3840 au) onto the source-subtracted background maps in 10 mass bins across 4 draws (~3800 synthetic cores per field), re-extract with getsf, and find the 90% recovery mass limit.
key_parameters: Gaussian FWHM = 3840 au; minimum separation > 2.5"; border exclusion = 5"; 10 flux bins (equivalent to 0.5-5 M_sun at 20 K, or 1-10 M_sun in W51-E); 4 draws per field (~3800 cores total); completeness threshold = 90%.
assumptions: Synthetic core fluxes converted to mass using the mean temperature of the cores extracted in the corresponding region.

recipe.goal: Fit the high-mass slope of the global CMF and quantify uncertainties and Salpeter tension
recipe.method: Fit a power-law PDF p(x) ∝ x^-α to the 330 bound cores above x_min = 1.64 M_sun (excluding W51-E) using Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) and the Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance in the powerlaw Python package, propagate uncertainties via 10^3 Monte Carlo realizations, and test tension with Salpeter (α = 2.35) via 10^5 synthetic draws.
key_parameters: x_min = 1.64 M_sun; n = 330 cores; 10^3 Monte Carlo trials with β ~ N(1.5, 0.2), T ~ N(T_core, σ_T), and Gaussian flux errors; 10^5 Salpeter synthetic trials.
assumptions: High-mass tail of the CMF follows a power-law distribution p(x) = C x^-α above x_min.

answer_key.quantity: CMF high-mass power-law slope α (direct MLE fit before Monte Carlo)

evidence.quote: From that subsample, we obtain a power-law index fit α = 2.11 ± 0.06 [8] .

answer_key.quantity: CMF high-mass power-law slope α (with Monte Carlo uncertainties)

evidence.quote: A power-law fit to the CMF of the sub-sample of cores above the 1.64 _M_ ⊙ completeness limit — 330 cores — through the maximum likelihood estimate technique yields a slope of 1.97 ± 0.06, significantly flatter than the 2.35 Salpeter slope.

We obtain a mean exponent value for the slope of the CMF of 1.97±0.06, where the uncertainty is the quadratic sum of the statistical uncertainty from Eq. 7 (σ ≃ 0.06) and from the uncertainties on the temperature, opacity index, and flux measurement uncertainties (σ ≃ 0.02).

answer_key.quantity: Statistical tension with the canonical Salpeter IMF slope (α = 2.35)

evidence.quote: Therefore, we report that the CMF in the protoclusters studied by ALMA-IMF is flatter than, and cannot reasonably be reconciled with the Salpeter-IMF slope to a 2.4σ level [9] .

score_reason: The input cleanest continuum maps and the complete intermediate/final core catalogs (with fluxes, sizes, spectral indices, PPMAP temperatures, and masses in Tables D.1-D.24 and on CDS/website) are publicly released, and the mass conversion, filtering criteria, and MLE fitting (via the open-source powerlaw package) are explicitly given by equations. Full end-to-end reproduction from the FITS images only lacks exact getsf/GExt2D configuration files.
rediscovery_reason: Both the ALMA-IMF cleanest continuum maps and the full extracted core catalogs are publicly available, and the main scientific results (core counts, core masses via Eq. 4, and the global CMF slope α = 1.97 ± 0.06 via the powerlaw package) are quantitative and can be directly reproduced.
